008package paint.shared.validate;
009
010import paint.shared.utils.TextFiles;
011import org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat;
012import org.apache.commons.csv.CSVParser;
013import org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord;
014import tech.tablesaw.api.ColumnType;
015
016import java.io.*;
017import java.time.LocalDateTime;
018import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter;
019import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatterBuilder;
020import java.time.temporal.ChronoField;
021import java.util.HashSet;
022import java.util.List;
023import java.util.Set;
024import java.util.stream.Collectors;
025
026import static paint.shared.utils.BooleanUtils.checkBooleanValue;
027
028/**
029 * Abstract superclass for all CSV file validators in PAINT.
030 * <p>
031 * Provides header, type, and optional value-validation mechanisms that are
032 * common across multiple experiment file formats.
033 * Concrete subclasses specify expected headers and types.
034 * </p>
035 */
036public abstract class AbstractFileValidator {
037
038    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
039    // INTERNAL STATE
040    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
041
042    /**
043     * Tracks which column type errors have already been reported to avoid duplicates.
044     */
045    private final Set<String> reportedTypeErrors = new HashSet<>();
046
047    /**
048     * Flexible timestamp parser supporting multiple formats with optional fractions.
049     */
050    private static final DateTimeFormatter FLEXIBLE_DATE_TIME = new DateTimeFormatterBuilder()
051            .appendPattern("[yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss][dd/MM/yyyy'T'HH:mm:ss]")
052            .optionalStart()
053            .appendFraction(ChronoField.NANO_OF_SECOND, 1, 9, true)
054            .optionalEnd()
055            .toFormatter();
056
057    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
058    // VALIDATION ENTRY POINTS
059    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
060
061    /**
062     * Validates both headers and row values of the specified CSV file.
063     *
064     * @param file        CSV file to validate
065     * @param checkValues whether to validate row values against expected types
066     * @return a {@link ValidationResult} containing all detected issues
067     */
068    public ValidationResult validate(File file, boolean checkValues) {
069        ValidationResult result = new ValidationResult();
070
071        CSVFormat format = CSVFormat.DEFAULT.builder()
072                .setDelimiter(',')
073                .setHeader()
074                .setSkipHeaderRecord(false)
075                .setIgnoreSurroundingSpaces(true)
076                .build();
077
078        try (Reader reader = TextFiles.newReader(file.toPath());
079             CSVParser parser = format.parse(reader)) {
080
081            List<String>    header  = parser.getHeaderNames();
082            List<CSVRecord> records = parser.getRecords();
083
084            validateHeader(header, result);
085
086            if (!checkValues || result.hasErrors()) {
087                return result; // Stop early if only header check or header invalid
088            }
089
090            ColumnType[] types            = getExpectedTypes();
091            boolean      reportedMismatch = false;
092
093            for (int i = 0; i < records.size(); i++) {
094                CSVRecord record = records.get(i);
095                String[] row = new String[header.size()];
096
097                for (int j = 0; j < header.size(); j++) {
098                    row[j] = record.get(j);
099                }
100
101                if (row.length != types.length) {
102                    if (!reportedMismatch) {
103                        result.addError("Row " + (i + 2) + " has " + row.length
104                                                + " values; expected " + types.length
105                                                + ". Possible formatting issue (e.g., extra/missing commas).");
106                        reportedMismatch = true;
107                    }
108                    continue;
109                }
110                rowMatchesTypes(row, types, header, i + 2, result);  // +2 because header = 1, data starts at 2
111            }
112        } catch (IOException e) {
113            result.addError("Error reading file: " + e.getMessage());
114        }
115
116        return result;
117    }
118
119    /**
120     * Validates both headers and values.
121     *
122     * @param file CSV file to validate
123     * @return {@link ValidationResult} describing validation results
124     */
125    public ValidationResult validate(File file) {
126        return validate(file, true);
127    }
128
129    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
130    // ABSTRACT DEFINITIONS
131    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
132
133    /**
134     * Subclasses implement header validation logic for a specific CSV schema.
135     *
136     * @param actualHeader header names read from the CSV
137     * @param result       result accumulator for recording mismatches
138     */
139    protected abstract void validateHeader(List<String> actualHeader, ValidationResult result);
140
141    /**
142     * Returns the expected column types for the CSV file.
143     *
144     * @return array of {@link ColumnType} values
145     */
146    protected abstract ColumnType[] getExpectedTypes();
147
148    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
149    // HELPER METHODS
150    // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
151
152    /**
153     * Compares expected and actual header sequences, recording mismatches.
154     *
155     * @param expected expected header names
156     * @param actual   actual header names
157     * @param result   validation result for error reporting
158     */
159    protected void headersMatch(List<String> expected, List<String> actual, ValidationResult result) {
160
161        // Return when the actual header is equal to the expected one
162        if (expected.equals(actual)) {
163            return;
164        }
165
166        // Find the headers that should be present (according to schema), but are not in the CSV.
167        List<String> missing = expected.stream()
168                .filter(h -> !actual.contains(h))
169                .collect(Collectors.toList());
170
171        // Find the headers that appear in the CSV, but are not expected.
172        List<String> unexpected = actual.stream()
173                .filter(h -> !expected.contains(h))
174                .collect(Collectors.toList());
175
176        if (missing.isEmpty() && unexpected.isEmpty()) {
177            // Elements match but order is wrong
178            result.addError("Header order mismatch: expected " + expected + " but found " + actual);
179            return;
180        }
181
182        // Create the error string
183        StringBuilder error = new StringBuilder("Header mismatch:");
184        if (!missing.isEmpty()) {
185            error.append("\n- Missing headers: ").append(missing);
186        }
187        if (!unexpected.isEmpty()) {
188            error.append("\n- Unexpected headers: ").append(unexpected);
189        }
190
191        // Append the error string to what there already was
192        result.addError(error.toString());
193    }
194
195    /**
196     * Checks whether all row values conform to expected column types.
197     *
198     * @param row      string array of CSV values
199     * @param types    expected column types
200     * @param headers  header names
201     * @param result   validation accumulator
202      */
203    protected void rowMatchesTypes(
204            String[] row,
205            ColumnType[] types,
206            List<String> headers,
207            int rowNumber,
208            ValidationResult result
209    ) {
210        for (int i = 0; i < types.length; i++) {
211
212            String value = row[i];
213            ColumnType type = types[i];
214
215            if (!canParse(value, type)) {
216
217                String colName = (headers.size() > i ? headers.get(i) : "Column " + (i + 1));
218                String key = colName + " type " + type.name();
219
220                // DIAGNOSTIC VALUE
221                result.addWarning(
222                        "Invalid value in column '" + colName +
223                                "' at row " + rowNumber +
224                                ": '" + value + "' (expected " + type.name() + ")"
225                );
226
227                // SINGLE SUMMARY ERROR per column/type
228                if (!reportedTypeErrors.contains(key)) {
229                    result.addError(
230                            "Some values in column '" + colName +
231                                    "' are invalid for type " + type.name() + "."
232                    );
233                    reportedTypeErrors.add(key);
234                }
235            }
236        }
237    }
238
239    /**
240     * Determines if a value can be parsed as the given column type.
241     *
242     * @param value raw string value
243     * @param type  expected type
244     * @return {@code true} if value is parseable or empty; otherwise {@code false}
245     */
246    private boolean canParse(String value, ColumnType type) {
247        if (value == null || value.trim().isEmpty()) {
248            return true;
249        }
250
251        try {
252            switch (type.name()) {
253                case "INTEGER":
254                    Integer.parseInt(value);
255                    break;
256                case "DOUBLE":
257                    Double.parseDouble(value);
258                    break;
259                case "BOOLEAN":
260                    String v = value.trim().toLowerCase();
261                    if (!checkBooleanValue(v)) {
262                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid boolean: " + value);
263                    }
264                    break;
265                case "LOCAL_DATE_TIME":
266                    LocalDateTime.parse(value, FLEXIBLE_DATE_TIME);
267                    break;
268                case "STRING":
269                    break;
270                default:
271                    return false;
272            }
273            return true;
274        } catch (Exception e) {
275            return false;
276        }
277    }
278}
